luke.12.p1.b1.text: In the meantime, a crowd of many thousands had gathered, so that they were trampling one another.

luke.12.p1.b2.text: “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

luke.12.p1.b3.text: what you have whispered in the inner rooms will be proclaimed from the housetops.

luke.12.p2.b1.text: I tell you, My friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that can do no more.

luke.12.p2.b2.text: Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? Yet not one of them is forgotten by God.

luke.12.p2.b3.text: And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.

luke.12.p3.b1.text: everyone who confesses Me before men, the Son of Man will also confess him before the angels of God.

luke.12.p3.b2.text: When you are brought before synagogues, rulers, and authorities, do not worry about how to defend yourselves or what to say.

luke.12.p3.b3.text: For at that time the Holy Spirit will teach you what you should say.”

luke.12.p4.b1.text: “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”

luke.12.p4.b2.text: “Man, who appointed Me judge or executor between you?”

luke.12.p4.b3.text: “Watch out! Guard yourselves against every form of greed, for one’s life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions.”

luke.12.p5.b1.text: “The ground of a certain rich man produced an abundance.

luke.12.p5.b2.text: ‘What shall I do, since I have nowhere to store my crops?’

luke.12.p5.b3.text: ‘This is what I will do: I will tear down my barns and will build bigger ones, …

luke.12.p5.b4.text: “You have plenty of good things laid up for many years. Take it easy. Eat, drink, and be merry!”

luke.12.p6.b1.text: ‘You fool! This very night your life will be required of you. Then who will own what you have accumulated?’

luke.12.p6.b2.text: This is how it will be for anyone who stores up treasure for himself but is not rich toward God.”

luke.12.p7.b1.text: “Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.

luke.12.p7.b2.text: Consider the ravens: They do not sow or reap, they have no storehouse or barn; yet God feeds them.

luke.12.p7.b3.text: Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?

luke.12.p8.b1.text: Consider how the lilies grow: They do not labor or spin.

luke.12.p8.b2.text: Yet I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these.

luke.12.p8.b3.text: the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, …

luke.12.p8.b4.text: But seek His kingdom, and these things will be added unto you.

luke.12.p9.b1.text: Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.

luke.12.p9.b2.text: Sell your possessions and give to the poor. Provide yourselves with purses that will not wear out, …

luke.12.p9.b3.text: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

luke.12.p10.b1.text: Be dressed for service and keep your lamps burning.

luke.12.p10.b2.text: when he comes and knocks, they can open the door for him at once.

luke.12.p10.b3.text: Truly I tell you, he will dress himself to serve and will have them recline at the table, and he himself will come and wait on them.

luke.12.p11.b1.text: If the homeowner had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have let his house be broken into.

luke.12.p11.b2.text: You also must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.”

luke.12.p12.b1.text: “Lord, … are You addressing this parable to us, or to everyone else as well?”

luke.12.p12.b2.text: “Who then is the faithful and wise manager, whom the master puts in charge of his servants to give them their portion at the proper time?

luke.12.p12.b3.text: Blessed is that servant whose master finds him doing so when he returns.

luke.12.p12.b4.text: Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.

luke.12.p13.b1.text: ‘My master will be a long time in coming,’

luke.12.p13.b2.text: … he begins to beat the menservants and maidservants, and to eat and drink and get drunk.

luke.12.p13.b3.text: The master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not anticipate. …

luke.12.p13.b4.text: From everyone who has been given much, much will be required; and from him who has been entrusted with much, even more will be demanded.

luke.12.p14.b1.text: I have come to ignite a fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!

luke.12.p14.b2.text: But I have a baptism to undergo, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!

luke.12.p15.b1.text: Do you think that I have come to bring peace to the earth? No, I tell you, but division.

luke.12.p15.b2.text: From now on, five in one household will be divided, three against two and two against three.

luke.12.p15.b3.text: father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother,

luke.12.p15.b4.text: mother-in-law against daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law.”

luke.12.p16.b1.text: “As soon as you see a cloud rising in the west, you say, ‘A shower is coming,’ and that is what happens.

luke.12.p16.b2.text: And when the south wind blows, you say, ‘It will be hot,’ and it is.

luke.12.p16.b3.text: You hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and sky. Why don’t you know how to interpret the present time?

luke.12.p17.b1.text: And why don’t you judge for yourselves what is right?

luke.12.p17.b2.text: Make every effort to reconcile with your adversary while you are on your way to the magistrate.

luke.12.p17.b3.text: Otherwise, he may drag you off to the judge, and the judge may hand you over to the officer, and the officer may throw you into prison.

luke.12.p17.b4.text: I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid the very last penny.”
